title: Gene regulation in prokaryotes (lac operon); Control of gene expression: transcription factors and epigenetics; Polygenic and environmental variation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: GR02#t1 term and clue written for the game; GR01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; GR01a#t2 term and clue written for the game; GR02#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: GR01a#N.2, GR01b#N.4, GR02#N.4, IN07#N.2, GR01a#N.4a, GR01b#N.12, GR02#N.9, IN07#N.9, GR01a#N.6, GR01a#N.11, GR01a#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Operon
items.clue: Group of genes transcribed together under shared control.

items.label: Gene expression
items.clue: Whole route from a stretch of DNA to a protein doing its job in the cell.

items.label: Transcription
items.clue: Step that makes mRNA; the main switch deciding whether a protein is made.

items.label: Promoter
items.clue: Site where RNA polymerase binds before transcribing the structural genes.

questions.stem: Developing red blood cells produce large amounts of the beta chain of haemoglobin, but liver cells produce none, although both cell types contain the gene. Which statement explains the difference?

options.text: Liver cells lost the gene when they differentiated, so they no longer contain the DNA sequence for the beta chain.
The gene is transcribed in developing red blood cells but not in liver cells, so liver cells make no mRNA for the protein.
Both cell types transcribe the gene, but only red blood cells translate the mRNA into the beta chain polypeptide.
Both cell types make the beta chain, but liver cells break the protein down as soon as it has been produced.

questions.stem: Blood cells from people living in a city with high levels of particulate air pollution were compared with blood cells from people living in an area with clean air. The pattern of methyl tags on the DNA of several genes differed between the two groups, but the base sequences of those genes were the same. Which conclusion is best supported by these findings?

options.text: The two groups must have differed genetically before any exposure to pollution
Air pollution acted as a mutagen, changing the genes in the blood cells
Air pollution altered gene expression without altering genotype
The altered tags will be inherited by the children of the exposed people

questions.explanation: Altered methyl tags with an unchanged base sequence is an environmental effect on gene expression: the expression pattern changed while the genotype did not.

questions.stem: Escherichia coli bacteria growing in a medium without lactose are transferred to a medium containing lactose. Within minutes they begin to synthesise beta-galactosidase, the enzyme that hydrolyses lactose. What causes this change in gene expression?

options.text: Lactose is the raw material from which the bacteria build the new enzyme
Lactose acts as a transcription factor, binding directly to the gene's promoter
Lactose stops the bacteria from transcribing the gene coding for the repressor
Lactose binds to the repressor protein, which releases the operator

questions.explanation: Lactose (as its isomer allolactose) binds to the lac repressor and changes its shape so that it no longer binds the operator. RNA polymerase can then transcribe the genes.

questions.stem: Identical twins have the same genotype. Two identical twins were raised apart, one in a sunny country on a good diet and the other in a cloudy country on a poor diet. Which of these traits are expected to be the same in both twins as adults: ABO blood group, adult height and skin colour?

options.text: ABO blood group, but neither adult height nor skin colour
ABO blood group and adult height, but not skin colour
ABO blood group and skin colour, though not adult height
ABO blood group, adult height and skin colour

questions.explanation: Identical twins have the same alleles, so ABO blood group, due to genotype only, is the same in both. Height depends on nutrition during growth and skin colour on sunlight, as well as on alleles, so both are expected to differ.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of yeast, protein P represses gene G by binding to a DNA sequence next to the promoter of gene G. A mutation changes this DNA sequence so that protein P can no longer bind to it. Which prediction about cells with this mutation is correct?

options.text: Protein G would have a different amino acid sequence, as gene G has mutated.
Gene G would be transcribed even with protein P present, as P no longer blocks it.
Gene G would no longer be transcribed, as protein P could not bind to switch it on.
The cells would make extra protein P so that it could still bind and repress gene G.

questions.stem: Female honeybee larvae in a hive are genetically alike. Larvae fed only on royal jelly develop into fertile queens; larvae switched to a diet of worker jelly develop into smaller, sterile workers. Which explanation is consistent with the understanding of gene expression?

options.text: Larvae fed worker jelly lose the genes that are needed for queen development
The diet alters epigenetic tags, so the two castes express different sets of the same genes
Royal jelly contains a mutagen that alters the base sequence of the larva's growth genes
The diet cannot cause the difference, so the caste of each larva must be fixed at fertilisation

questions.stem: A mutant strain of E. coli makes a lac repressor that still binds the operator normally, but can no longer bind lactose. What happens when these bacteria are given lactose?

options.text: The enzymes are made as normal, because lactose can still bind the operator and switch the genes on.
The enzymes are not made, because the repressor stays on the operator even with lactose present.
The enzymes are made when lactose is present, but they have altered amino acid sequences.
The enzymes are made, because lactose stops the bacteria transcribing the repressor gene.

questions.stem: Human skin colour varies continuously across a population, whereas ABO blood group falls into four separate classes. Which explanation of this difference is correct?

options.text: Skin colour is controlled by one gene with a very large number of alleles, whereas the blood group gene has only three alleles
Skin colour is determined by the environment only, with no genetic contribution, whereas blood group is determined by genotype only
Both are continuous variables, since each can be sorted into several categories; skin colour simply has more of them
Skin colour depends on several genes and on sunlight, giving many grades; blood group depends on one gene with discrete alleles

questions.stem: Oestrogen is a steroid hormone that passes through the plasma membrane of its target cells. How does oestrogen alter the pattern of gene expression in these cells?

options.text: It binds to a receptor protein, and the hormone–receptor complex acts as a transcription factor
It binds directly to the promoters of its target genes in place of a transcription factor
It activates enzymes already in the cell by binding to their active sites, without any transcription
It adds methyl tags to cytosine in the promoters of target genes, switching them on

questions.stem: Cytosine bases in the DNA of a gene's promoter become methylated. What is the effect on the gene?

options.text: Translation of the gene's mRNA is blocked, because ribosomes cannot read methylated codons
The base sequence of the gene is altered, so a different polypeptide is produced from it
Transcription of the gene is increased, because the methyl tag marks it for expression
Transcription of the gene downstream is repressed, so it is not expressed

questions.explanation: Methylation of cytosine in a promoter represses transcription and therefore expression of the gene downstream, without any change in the base sequence.

questions.stem: In a skin cell, the promoter of gene G is methylated and the gene is not expressed. The cell divides by mitosis. What is the most likely state of gene G in the daughter cells, and why?

options.text: Not expressed, because the methyl tags remained in place through mitosis
Expressed, because epigenetic tags are lost whenever DNA is replicated
Not expressed, because the methylation has changed the base sequence of the gene
Not expressed in the person's children, because the tags pass to offspring

questions.explanation: Tags such as promoter methylation can remain in place during mitosis, so the daughter cells inherit the same pattern of gene expression. The base sequence of gene G is unchanged.
